text:
The Team USA three-time Olympic medallist clipped a gate and fell to the ground in pain, in what could be the last race of her legendary career.
Just a week after suffering a serious knee injury, Lindsey Vonn's Olympic Milano Cortina 2026 Alpine skiing downhill dreams came to an end, as she crashed out of the race on Sunday (8 February).
The three-time Olympic medallist screamed in pain as she fell to the ground after clipping a gate on a right-hand turn just seconds into her run.
The crowd fell silent for a full minute and her coach Aksel Lund Svindal looked on very concerned. The race was halted for more than 10 minutes before Vonn was airlifted away to Codivilla Hospital in Cortina for medical evaluation.
"It's hard to believe. We just hope she will be OK," said her sister Karin Kildow to NBC.
The U.S. Alpine skiing legend suffered a ruptured ACL, bone bruising, and meniscal damage on 30 January in the later-cancelled Crans-Montana downhill,
However, after making the decision to race in Italy, she lined up 13th on the start list for the women's downhill. 
The crash at the Tofane Alpine Skiing Centre is most likely to bring her Olympic campaign to a sad end. It could also be the last race of the legendary skier's career. 
Vonn is one of the most successful Alpine skiers in history, having won gold in downhill and bronze in super-G at Vancouver 2010, as well as bronze in downhill at PyeongChang 2018.
